title: input-method-relay: Fix NULL deref in keyboard grab destroy handler
description:
## Problem

`handle_im_keyboard_grab_destroy()` in `src/input-method-relay.c` uses the
signal data as `struct wlr_input_method_keyboard_grab_v2 *` unconditionally.

wlroots changed that signal to be emitted with `NULL` data in 0.20.0, see
wlroots commit [06275103](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/wlroots/wlroots/-/commit/06275103f249cd2954630e59383342e102a6c1a3)
("input-method-v2: Destroy keyboard grab before input method"), which
also made `input_method->events.destroy`, `input_method->events.commit`
and `input_method_manager_v2::events.destroy` pass `NULL`.

phoc 0.55.1 already pins wlroots 0.20.0 in `subprojects/wlroots.wrap`,
so every time an input method tears down its keyboard grab the
compositor dies with a SIGSEGV at `NULL + offsetof(..., keyboard)`
(`NULL+0x10` on aarch64) and the whole session gets restarted.

Observed on a Qualcomm SM8750 phone/tablet running phoc 0.55.1 with
wlroots 0.20.0 (Alpine 3.24, aarch64):

```
Thread 1 "phoc" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault.
#0  handle_im_keyboard_grab_destroy ()
#1  wl_signal_emit_mutable ()
#2  wlr_input_method_keyboard_grab_v2_destroy ()
#3  wl_client_destroy ()
```

Disassembly of the shipped binary matches the theory exactly:

```
/usr/bin/phoc  0x76000 <handle_im_keyboard_grab_destroy>:
  76010:  ldr  x1, [sp, #24]      ; x1 = data
  76014:  ldr  x0, [x1, #16]      ; data->keyboard  ⇒ fault at 0x10
```

Since a seat only accepts a single input method, this was easy to hit on a
device that ships an on-screen keyboard *and* a regular input method
engine: the second one gets `unavailable`, but the grab teardown path is
the same, so the compositor crashed as soon as an input method released
its grab.

## Fix

The grab is still attached to the input method while the signal is
emitted (wlroots clears `input_method->keyboard_grab` only after the
emit), so look it up there when `data` is `NULL`. This keeps the original
behaviour (forwarding the modifier state to the focused client) instead
of just dropping it, and remains compatible with wlroots versions that
still pass the grab as data.

## Testing

Verified on the affected device by building phoc 0.55.1 natively with
`-Dembed-wlroots=enabled` (wlroots 0.20.0) and A/B-ing against the
distro binary.

A minimal client (`zwp_input_method_manager_v2.get_input_method()` →
`zwp_input_method_v2.grab_keyboard()` → release) is the only reliable
trigger — starting/stopping a real OSK is not, because
squeekboard never grabs the keyboard and a second input method gets
`unavailable` and therefore never creates a grab.

| arm | slot state | result |
|---|---|---|
| unpatched phoc | `acquired` | **CRASH 2/2** |
| unpatched phoc | `unavailable` | survived 2/2 (no grab created) |
| patched phoc | `acquired` | **survived 5/5** |

Minimal reproducer (also useful as a test case):

```sh
wayland-scanner client-header input-method-unstable-v2.xml im-v2.h
wayland-scanner private-code  input-method-unstable-v2.xml im-v2.c
cc -O0 -g -o imtest imtest.c im-v2.c -lwayland-client

pkill -x fcitx5; pkill -x squeekboard      # the slot must be free
WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0 ./imtest grab    # grabs, then releases after 2s
pgrep -ax phoc                             # unpatched: pid changed / gone
```

I can attach `imtest.c` or turn it into a `examples/` client (or a
`tests/` case) if you prefer — happy to adjust the approach.

title: incorrect key used when retrieving a sequence state
description:
phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state() uses the wrong key when looking up priv-\>points. The hash table is indexed by PhocEventSequence \*, but the function uses the PhocGesture \*self pointer as the lookup key. As a result, the sequence state cannot be retrieved correctly and PHOC_EVENT_SEQUENCE_NONE is returned instead of the actual state.

In phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state(), the priv-\>points hash table is indexed by PhocEventSequence \*.\
\
When a point is added, it is stored using sequence as the key:\
\
g_hash_table_insert (priv-\>points, sequence, data);\
\
However, phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state() uses self as the key when looking up the corresponding PointData:\
\
data = g_hash_table_lookup (priv-\>points, self);\
\
Since self is a PhocGesture \* rather than a PhocEventSequence \*, the lookup cannot find the PointData associated with the sequence. As a result, the function returns PHOC_EVENT_SEQUENCE_NONE instead of the actual state of the sequence.\
\
The lookup should use sequence instead:\
\
data = g_hash_table_lookup (priv-\>points, sequence);\
\
This allows phoc_gesture_get_sequence_state() to correctly retrieve the PointData associated with the requested sequence and return its state.

So this solve some bugs.

Fixes #434
